I have more now. I’ve always enjoyed dressing up. Always. I’m not uncomfortable in a shirt and tie. I’m at my best in a shirt and tie. I love dressing up. That comes from my boyhood, going with my mother to church where you had to wear a suit. People ask me all the time, “Hey, man, ain’t you uncomfortable in a suit?” No, I’m at my most comfortable when I’m in a suit.

I always loved dressing up, but what Elly [Karamoh, Harvey’s stylist] brought to me was the different things to wear: Balenciaga, Bottega Veneta, Kiton, Prada, Gucci, the newer Tom Ford. The looks had lots of different colors, because I was always a color-driven guy, but I lost that trying to dress for my talk show.

How many closets do you have?

I have two main closets. One closet is mostly stage clothes. It’s my man cave. [Editor’s note: Harvey has a three-story man cave on his property, separate from his main house.] This is the only space that I’m allowed to decorate and do anything I want with. In that big-ass house, this is all I have control over. I don’t have a say-so in a light bulb in that other house. But over here I can do the Steve Harvey thing.

What do you think your influence has been on fashion?

Pharrell was sitting next to me at an event I had out in the country, and he said, “Hey, man, you got these young dudes in a headlock with your fashions.” I really think I played a role in guys changing their fashions now, because if you look at the BET Awards and the Grammys, they ain’t wearing T-shirts no more. They’re starting to dress up because I’ve never given up on dressing up. A lot of young cats have called me and said, “Hey, man, can I use your stylist?” —Cam Wolf

Brunello Cucinelli

Cashmere Philosopher King, 73
Solomeo, Italy

Paolo di Lucente

Is your wardrobe entirely from your label?

My current wardrobe is only made up of my brand’s clothes, but [the company archive has] a 5,000-square-meter warehouse where I store about 60,000 items that I’ve collected over the years. I think I deserve some money from Ralph Lauren, because I’ve bought so many pieces from him.

For my personal items, I still have them all, from when I was 25 years old onwards. I have a T-shirt with “Los Angeles” written on it that was given to me by a girl whom I fancied—she was an unrequited love, but I still remember her. And do you know why I never throw away any piece? Because every piece basically epitomizes a moment of your life. I envisage one day my grandchildren looking through my wardrobe and saying, “That’s what my grandfather used to wear when he was young.”

Is keeping your closet clean and organized important to you?

Alexander Pope said, “Order is heaven’s first law.” So I’m very tidy as a person, very orderly. When I shine my shoes, I always do it myself because my wife doesn’t do a proper job. That’s the way I am. I like to see all my ties together, all my footwear together, everything perfectly tidy.

This is also very important to do when you’re young: Every single piece of clothing has a label with the date in it. It’s really nice to know exactly when you bought something. Maybe somebody says to me, “Oh, have you put on weight?” “No, look—this is from 1991!” —Y.G.

Paolo di Lucente

London, England

Francesco Nazardo

Do you collect any of your work from Louis Vuitton or Dior?

I have a few pieces of Vuitton. The rest I gave all away, apart from one pair of shoes from Dior. I never designed for myself, and once I’ve finished with something I become bored looking at it.

You’ve said you don’t like to take too long to get ready in the mornings.

I normally lay my outfit out on the carpet in my dressing room the day before. The less things I have to think about myself when I’m working, the more time I’m focused on work. I’m not one of those people that are used to fucking chat, chat, chat about their work. I just get on with it. Because I think the people that chat about their work all the time aren’t doing their work properly.

I notice you have quite a few Hermès Cargo Birkins.

Yeah, I like Cargoes and I like Kelly Dolls. I go through phases of wearing the same thing all the time, and I just find having a nice bag is a way of breaking things up.

Would you say you’re a type-A person?

What’s that? —Zoë Kezia

Francesco Nazardo

Leon Thomas III

Grammy-Winning Hitmaker, 33
Los Angeles, California

Aaron Sinclair. Grooming by Vicky Garcia using Armani Beauty. Barbering by Gary “GQ” Bonney.

Are you one of those people who has the same piece in different fabrics?

Pretty much. When I first got signed by my mentor Ty Dolla $ign, he was like, “Think about your wardrobe as if you were about to be drawn as a cartoon character. What is the silhouette that somebody could draw that makes sense?” And that kind of just clicked in my head. And since then, I’ve been really making sure that we stay close to the kind of cuts that really cater to my body type. I do my best to switch it up, though. You don’t want to wear the same thing every day, but you want to find a way to tell the same story a bunch of different ways.

Do you collect anything?

I have a pretty extensive collection of paperboy hats. It’s not like a traditional Kangol. Reminds me of the ’70s. I got about a good 20 or 30 hats just like that, so I can switch it up any color, any day and still stay in my silhouette.

Where do you get your hats?

I’m going to have to gatekeep this one, man. They going to be buying up all my hats. —R.A.

A man of the people.

Are you particular about what you use to organize your closet?

Brooklyn, New York

Ryan Duffin

So your closet is in your basement?

It’s like the laundry room that has become my dressing room, like I’m a Victorian wife. It’s a place of peace for me. I spend my whole fucking day dealing with things that I can’t control, and I can go into my room with my clothes and put things together.

What do you have the most of?

I have 90 million graphic tees. I have so many gay graphic tees. Every diva. There’s not a gay bar in a small town that I do not have a fucking T-shirt from.

And then, unfortunately, I have so many variations of black GOTs—“going-out tops.” It’s like, black asymmetrical GOT, black mesh GOT, black shiny GOT, black sparkly GOT.
